decisions.action: satisfy polling_rdma_output_line_is_not_zero() with a __weak no-op instead of deleting the call or disabling MTCMOS
decisions.reason: the vendor defines it in the display driver (drivers/misc/mediatek/video/mt6768/dispsys/ddp_rdma_ex.c:1588) as a wait on DISP_RDMA_OUT_LINE_CNT before an mm_sel re-parent on a command-mode panel; the video subtree is not ported, so the symbol is undefined at link. mm_polling() is already gated on subsys_is_on(SYS_DIS), so with no display driver bound there is no RDMA in flight to wait for; MT_MTCMOS_ENABLE=0 (the vendor's bringup config) would have discarded the file's purpose. The display port's strong definition overrides the stub. Stated loss if display lands without restoring the link: transient panel underflow on mid-frame mm_sel switches.

decisions.action: rename the header guard to __DRV_CLK_MTK_V1_H when transplanting
decisions.reason: 5.15's drivers/clk/mediatek/clk-mtk.h uses the guard __DRV_CLK_MTK_H that this vendor header also claims, and clk-mt6768-pg.c includes both; with the original guard whichever came first silently swallowed the other, which would have looked like a compile error in whichever header lost.

decisions.action: do not port the vendor legacy clock manager (nor clkdbg/clkchk)
decisions.reason: it is the pre-CCF manager that COMMON_CLK_MT6768 replaces and it registers the same DT nodes; porting both would give two providers per node. clk-mt6768.c references none of those files, so dropping them is not a semantic loss for the CCF path - but it is why the BSP's pericfg clock gating (which lived in clkmgr/clkbuf, not in DT phandles) has no 5.15 counterpart, recorded as the peri_clks gap.

decisions.action: audit clock enablement by resolving the DTB's flat clock cells against the driver's registered IDs, per provider domain
decisions.reason: 'the driver compiles and the symbol is on' says nothing about whether the provider can answer the board. Three tool bugs had to be fixed to make the number trustworthy, each of which would have produced a false all-clear or a false alarm: dtc -O dts prefixes nodes with their label ('pericfg: pericfg@10003000 {'), so a name-only regex lost the providers and made every reference look dangling; '#clock-cells' needs '#' in the property regex; multi-string compatibles print as one quoted string separated by \0 and must be split. Domain attribution also has to include mux/divider/factor tables, not just *_clks[], or topckgen reads as 5/65 registered when it is 65/65.

Vendor MT6768 PMIC-wrap map agrees with mainline's mt8183 table on all 43 comparable registers (0 differing) and with mt6765 on only 6 of 20 (RDDMY/HARB_HPRIO/MAN_CMD/WACS0_EN/INIT_DONE2/TIMER_EN/DCM all shifted). Offsets for every register pwrap_mt8183_init_soc_specific() writes were checked individually. MT6768 also has P2P/MD32 masters in its DTB, so that init applies.

Taken from the vendor's own MT6768 init (pwrap_hal.c:901,913) instead of MT8183's 0x3fa75/0xeef7ffff: the arbiter mask differs in bit 4 (which bus masters may reach the PMIC), so reusing MT8183's value would have been an invention with real consequences.

decisions.action: deliberate omission: PWRAP_CAP_DCM not set for mt6768
decisions.reason: MT6768 has DCM_EN/DCM_DBC_PRD at 0x1D0/0x1D8, which mt8183_regs does not describe; setting the cap would send the generic DCM path to offset 0. Cost is a missing debounce-counter diagnostic, not a wrong register write.

decisions.action: port: 'mediatek,mt6358-pmic' alias in of_slave_match_tbl and mt6397_of_match
decisions.reason: pwrap_probe() returns -EINVAL unless np->child matches its slave table, and the MFD must match the same node to create cells. The alias adds no behaviour: this board's PMIC is an MT6358 (vendor pwrap_hal.h: '#define MTK_PLATFORM_MT6358 1', node name, and the MT6358 EINT list in the DT).

5.15's mt6577_auxadc.c matches mt2701/mt2712/mt6765/mt7622/mt8173 only. The driver compiles but will not bind; battery temperature/Ra stay without a 5.15 provider. Needs the same offset-level comparison against the vendor's AUXADC block before an alias is justified - deliberately not guessed, because this path feeds charging.

decisions.action: fix: duplicate SND_SOC_MTK_BTCVSD Kconfig definition removed
decisions.reason: My ASoC Kconfig transplant (e5462a25cb) added a 'bool' copy of a symbol vanilla 5.15 already declares as 'tristate'; kconfig warned 'ignoring type redefinition' on every pass and kept the first type, overriding mainline's. Nothing selects the symbol, so removal is a pure defect fix (verified: 1 definition, 0 warnings from olddefconfig).

decisions.action: measurement: DTB sizes must be forced-rebuilt and labelled
decisions.reason: Two published causes of the 122,474 vs 89,053 mt6768.dtb difference were wrong. A forced rebuild gives 122,474 in both trees with a node set identical to the reference decompile; 89,053 was an artifact of my own experiment whose make exited rc=2 mid-rule. clkaudit.py now records inputs.dtb_provenance (size, sha256, sources newer than the DTB), warns on staleness and supports --require-fresh (exit 2). hwenable.py should get the same - recorded as a gap, not done.

decisions.action: correction: regulators do not need DT reg-encoding on MT6358
decisions.reason: mt6358-regulator.c registers MT6358_MAX_REGULATOR descriptors from static tables and binds as the MFD cell; no of_match_table, no per-regulator 'reg = <shift width mask>' property. My earlier claim that regulators could not bind from this DTB was based on the mt6323/mt6397 binding and is retracted.

It depends on MFD_MT6397, so scripts/config --enable was silently reverted by olddefconfig all along; an earlier note called it 'enabled but blocked at probe'. Now =y, which is only possible because the MFD was enabled first.

Not a family guess: the vendor's own drivers/iio/adc/mt6577_auxadc.c:560 maps this exact string to mt6765_compat, and mainline's variant struct is only two behaviour flags, whose values match the DTB's mediatek,cali-* properties.

decisions.action: port: transplant mt635x-auxadc_v1.c (PMIC MT6358 ADC) + MFD cell
decisions.reason: Mainline has no provider for 'mediatek,mt6358-auxadc'. The board's own 4.19 defconfig builds MT635X_AUXADC (v1), not MEDIATEK_MT635X_AUXADC, so v1 is the variant this hardware uses. Adaptations limited to struct mt6397_chip (mainline's own convention for this PMIC), the PMIC-chip Kconfig guard rebound to the driver's symbol, and 193 register defines copied verbatim from the vendor header by compiler-driven selection.

It is legacy-consumer registration (convert/cali callbacks, efuse calibration init, MDRT debug, cust_setting parsing, one VBIF28 sample), not PMIC programming; porting it means the vendor PMIC helper stack. Consequences written into the file and the docs: Vbat uncalibrated, Vbat_temp untrustworthy, and the exported auxadc_set_convert_fn()/auxadc_set_cali_fn() stay as the seam for the charging port.

decisions.action: port: mt6358-regulator per-rdev of_node via of_regulator_match()
decisions.reason: Without config.of_node every rdev inherits the MFD cell node, so consumer *-supply phandles (e.g. MSDC0's vmmc-supply = <&ldo_vemc>) match no regulator and defer forever. Match names are the driver's own desc.name strings; 41/41 of them exist as children in this DTB (42 children, ldo_va09 unmatched). of_regulator_match() returns a count and tolerates absent children, so other MT6358 boards keep prior behaviour.

Every field of the vendor's mt6768_compat equals mainline's mt6779_compat (clk_div_bits 12, hs400_tune false, pad_tune_reg MSDC_PAD_TUNE0, async_fifo, data_tune, busy_check, stop_clk_fix, enhance_rx, support_64g); the vendor struct simply predates recheck_sdio_irq, which mt6779_compat sets false. Clock names and the second reg resource in the DTB match what the driver requests (source/hclk/source_cg + top_base); the three clock ids decode to CLK_TOP_MSDC50_0 / CLK_IFR_MSDC0 / CLK_IFR_MSDC0_SRC, all registered by the ported clock provider.

decisions.action: declined: no I2C enablement this round
decisions.reason: The board DTB's nine i2cN nodes are the BSP's legacy hardware description (mediatek,i2c, vendor props, no #address-cells/#size-cells), i.e. not I2C adapters, and neither mainline's nor the vendor's own i2c-mt65xx matches 'mediatek,i2c'. Enabling CONFIG_I2C_MT65XX would create enabled-but-nonfunctional drivers; the prerequisite is a documented binding decision.

decisions.action: open: Image.gz-dtb packages a DTB built without the board DTS_CPPFLAGS
decisions.reason: Measured: dtbs -> 6 -DCONFIG flags, 163,417-byte intermediate, 122,474-byte DTB, 413 compatible nodes; packaging path -> 0 flags, 118,235 bytes, 89,053 bytes, 399 nodes, M4U/IOMMU blocks gone. Fixed by choosing the shipped DTB shape first (the +14 nodes drive vendor-only blocks), so this is recorded with the numbers rather than patched on a guess.

decisions.round: earlier (re-filed from a stray top-level key)
decisions.decision: reverted the ported hunks on upstream-only MediaTek board DTS (mt6755-evb.dts, mt6795-evb.dts, mt6797-evb.dts, mt6797-x20-dev.dts, mt2712e.dtsi, ...). The vendor 4.19 board trees rewrite their #include lines to point at downstream-only .dtsi files, so applying those hunks broke 17 of the 521 upstream DTB builds. None of these boards is the device: the even board tree is a separate, vendor-new file (see DTS plan).
decisions.why: kept at base: porting vendor hunks onto board DTS files this device does not use adds risk without benefit; the same holds for the two extra files that round touched
decisions.evidence: reverted hunks under arch/arm64/boot/dts/ for non-mt6768 MediaTek boards; verified by re-diffing against base
decisions.status: recorded; normalized into the decisions list this round so the file has one shape

decisions.decision: Fix the per-target DTB divergence by moving the board's DTS_CPPFLAGS into arch/arm64/boot/dts/mediatek/dts-cppflags.mk, included by BOTH the board dts Makefile and arch/arm64/boot/Makefile under CONFIG_ARCH_MEDIATEK.
decisions.why: The %.dtb rule lives in scripts/Makefile.lib:355 and its recipe ends with the directory-local $(DTS_CPPFLAGS) (:229), so naming the .dtb from arch/arm64/boot builds it without the board's -DCONFIG_* flags. Depending on the phony `dtbs` cannot fix it (the two cmd strings still differ, so if_changed rebuilds per target and image content becomes build-order dependent); global -D injection would touch every vendor's .dts and dirty unrelated .cmd state. One shared fragment makes both paths emit identical bytes.
decisions.evidence: before: 6 vs 0 -D flags in .mt6768.dtb.cmd, 122,474 vs 89,053 B, 413 vs 399 compatible-bearing nodes. after: one stable 122,474 B file (md5 a2522a615fd6) across dtbs/.dtb/Image.gz-dtb/dtbs; DTB byte-identical inside Image.gz-dtb at 10,603,132; Image.gz-dtb 11,063,228 -> 11,096,649 B with Image unchanged; build-33: 0 errors, 0 make failures, 7,371 objects, 840 .ko
decisions.status: implemented + measured; no board, so no boot claim

decisions.decision: Recompute every DT-derived report from the DTB as packaged, and pin mkbootimg's --boot-id to the recorded value when packing so verify can assert byte equality instead of header plausibility.
decisions.why: Before 0077 the audit input and the shipped DTB were different files, which made every 'node X exists' statement ambiguous. An unpinned --boot-id randomises each pack (measured: ef599039dd4495b6 vs 23e3c26b8a1412ad), so the round-trip gate could not compare hashes; with it pinned, boot.img and boot.img.dump.repack are byte-identical and the extracted dtb section equals the built file exactly.
decisions.evidence: hwenable.py on the packaged DTB: 413 nodes / 339 distinct / 21 bound / 15 enabled / 4 enableable / 318 driverless; clkaudit --require-fresh passes; dtc round-trip byte-identical 122,474 B; dtbo.img repacked with mkdtboimg --page_size=4096 -> same header (371,235 B, 5 entries)

decisions.decision: Answer 'how does the stock kernel reach those buses' from source before deciding anything, and leave I2C un-enabled meanwhile (user chose 'investigate the stock path first').
decisions.why: The gap looked like a missing compatible; it is not. even_defconfig builds CONFIG_I2C_MTK=y (i2c-mtk.c), whose of_match has 'mediatek,i2c' and which uses i2c_add_numbered_adapter + per-node ioconfig props (pu_cfg/rsel_cfg/eh_cfg/gpio_start/cg_bit), so the DT deliberately omits #address-cells/#size-cells and has no i2c pin groups at all. Corrected two earlier claims here: the vendor tree does match 'mediatek,i2c' (in i2c-mtk.c, not i2c-mt65xx.c), and mainline's mt65xx register layout for this IP is offset-identical to the BSP's (mt_i2c_regs_v1[] vs I2C_REGS_OFFSET; DMA blocks too), with mainline's mandatory clocks 'main'/'dma' already in the node and no pinctrl requirement in 5.15.
decisions.evidence: even_defconfig:2822; i2c-mtk.c:1641,1834-1835,1541-1555; i2c-mtk.h:43+,145+; portwork 5.15 i2c-mt65xx.c:111+(regs v1),86-96(DMA),409-416(match),1255-1273(clock gets); board DT i2c0@11007000 (dump:2672) with clock-names main/dma; grep: 0 i2c pinctrl groups, 21 'i2c' mentions total
decisions.status: investigated and documented; enablement deferred to the touch round with two written-up routes (additive DT cells+pin groups with mainline host, or vendor host verbatim)

decisions.decision: Before writing any SMI/M4U code, measure the subsystem against the packaged DTB and the clock audit; implement only S1 (clock-provider resolution) under the current constraints and hold S2/S3 for sign-off.
decisions.why: Three measured facts reshape the plan: (a) m4u@10205000 exists only in the `make dtbs`-shaped DTB, i.e. commit 0077 is what made this subsystem describable at all; (b) every SMI/M4U clock cell names a provider node the ported clk driver does not bind (mmsys_config 37 refs, scpsys 23, camsys 8, imgsys syscon@15020000 5, venc_gcon 4, vdec_gcon 2 - clkaudit's unresolved_provider 22), and scpsys shares its reg base with infracfg_ao, so the fix is provider-node wiring with the BSP's own cell numbering rather than new clock ids (guessing them is prohibited); (c) the DT has ZERO 'iommus' consumers, so a mainline-style IOMMU would exist for nobody to use, while the vendor stack needs vendor clients. Enabling SMI/M4U therefore cannot be delivered as a standalone functional step; S1 (22 -> 0 unresolved refs, driver-only) is the shared prerequisite.
decisions.evidence: dts/mt6768.packaged.dts.dump (4,546 lines) vs dts/mt6768.dts.dump (4,288): mediatek,m4u 1 vs 0, iommus 0 vs 0; smi node verbatim block in report/hardware-enablement.md; report/clkaudit.json totals {refs:234, registered:212, unresolved_provider:22, foreign_numbering:0}
decisions.status: assessment recorded; S1 proposed for the next round, S2/S3 need a decision (vendor-stack-only SMI vs lifting the no-DT-surgery rule for iommus/#dma-cells)

decisions.decision: Close the SMI 'clock provider gap' by fixing bin/clkaudit.py instead of the kernel: the 22 unresolved refs were the audit failing to attribute the mediatek,scpsys provider, which the ported clk-mt6768-pg.c already registers.
decisions.why: The instruction was to resolve the providers 'using the existing 5.15 clk-mt6768 framework and verified BSP cell-to-ID mappings, not the legacy clkmgr architecture'. Checking the premise first showed there was nothing to add: of_clk_add_provider() is called on the scpsys node at clk-mt6768-pg.c:3610 with scp_clks[]'s 13 ids (SCP_SYS_MD1..SCP_SYS_VDEC = 0..12, no holes, sized by SCP_NR_SYSS 13), and every DT cell in the set {1,3,4,5,7,8,9,10,11,12} is both in range and semantically right for its consumer (larb1->VDEC, larb2->ISP, larb3->CAM, larb4->VENC, gpufreq->MFG x3, consys->CONN). Writing a second provider for the same hardware would have double-registered clocks; the honest fix was the audit.
decisions.evidence: before: totals {refs:234, registered:212, unresolved_provider:22}; after: {refs:234, registered:234, unresolved_provider:0, foreign_numbering:0, header_id_not_registered:0, cross_domain_name_collisions:0}; scpsys node verbatim (#clock-cells = <1>, compatible "mediatek,scpsys\0syscon", phandle 0x27) from dts/mt6768.packaged.dts.dump; include/dt-bindings/clock/mt6768-clk.h:398-411
decisions.status: closed as a tool fix; no kernel source changed, so build-33 remains the reference build

decisions.decision: Give clkaudit.py three capabilities instead of a one-off exception: a second id family (SCP_SYS_*), a provider/compatible-to-table map that spans multiple --driver files, and per-row unresolved_refs in both JSON and markdown.
decisions.why: Each of the three was load-bearing for the wrong conclusion: the header parser matched only CLK_* so pg's cells were nameless; driver_tables() read one .c so scp_clks[] was invisible; PROVIDER_DOMAIN had no scpsys entry so its refs were 'unresolved'. Most importantly, the aggregate count with no rows is what let the claim survive two rounds - the moment the rows existed, the provider lookup answered immediately. Fixing all three keeps the tool from re-deriving the same class of error on mt6779/mt6785-style trees.
decisions.evidence: bin/clkaudit.py header_ids()/driver_tables() patterns now (?:CLK|SCP_SYS)_; PROVIDER_DOMAIN['mediatek,scpsys'] = 'SCP_SYS' with ARRAY_FOR_DOMAIN['SCP_SYS'] = ('scp_clks',); --driver is nargs='+'; markdown gained a legend (zero-cell refs count as classified but not as refs; cell numbers are per-domain and must not be compared across rows) and the unresolved table
decisions.status: implemented and re-run against the packaged DTB

decisions.decision: Record the measured S2/S3 input and recommend the vendor SMI/M4U stack, sequenced inside the display/video round with zero DT edits; do not enable CONFIG_MEDIATEK_SMI/CONFIG_MTK_IOMMU, do not add iommus/#dma-cells, and leave the M4U architecture decision open as instructed.
decisions.why: even_defconfig sets MTK_M4U=y (:1740), MTK_SMI=y (:4621), MTK_SMI_EXT=y (:1810), IOMMU_IOVA=y (:4462): the stock device runs drivers/misc/mediatek/m4u/mt6768 (3,074 lines in m4u_hw.c) + drivers/misc/mediatek/smi, and that SMI looks clocks up by name (mmdvfs_mgr_v3.c:813 of_clk_get_by_name, mtk-smi-dbg.c:691 devm_clk_get(name)), which is what the DT's per-larb names ('scp-isp','mm-img','img-larb2') exist for. The mainline alternative needs per-larb clock-names apb/smi + mediatek,smi (mtk-smi.c:332-350), a mediatek,LARB list on the m4u node (mtk_iommu.c:876-881) and iommus on clients - while the DTB has 0 iommus properties and its only clients (video/mt6768: 16 files referencing m4u; ccu/src: 31) call the vendor API. mt6779_data (:1049) is not a drop-in either (larbid_remap to larb 10 vs this SoC's five).
decisions.evidence: all of the above greps run on /home/user/portwork/build and /home/user/Zenium_Kernel this round; report/hardware-enablement.md carries the three-fact section
decisions.status: assessment recorded for the deferred decision; nothing enabled, no DT touched

decisions.decision: Port the vendor MT6768 SMI substrate by extracting the CONFIG_MTK_SMI_EXT half of the BSP's drivers/memory/mtk-smi.c into drivers/memory/mtk-smi-mt6768.c (plus a trimmed copy of the two smi_bus_* wrappers from drivers/misc/mediatek/smi/smi_drv.c), enabled by CONFIG_MTK_SMI_MT6768. Do NOT enable 5.15's mainline SMI/IOMMU path for this, and do not touch the DT.
decisions.why: The user fixed the route as 'vendor MT6768 SMI/M4U substrate first' and forbade converting the DT to mainline IOMMU bindings unless display/video clients prove it necessary. Inventory showed the mainline driver cannot serve this DT without edits (it asks for per-larb clock names apb/smi/gals and a common->larb mediatek,smi phandle topology, and its mt6779 larb data does not describe five larbs), while the vendor SMI_EXT code reads exactly what this DT carries: it iterates the node's own clock-names with of_property_for_each_string() and takes the device id from mediatek,smi-id. The obvious-looking BSP file drivers/misc/mediatek/smi/smi_drv.c is the wrong source - only 1,548 lines, but it is the BWC/monitor wrapper whose includes drag sspm IPI, aee.h, memory/mediatek/emi.h, emi_mbw.h, mmprofile and mmdvfs/PMQOS; the union of names its mt6768 headers export shows M4U and the video stack call just smi_bus_prepare_enable/smi_bus_disable_unprepare/smi_get_dev_num plus the SMI_EXT clock API, so that is what was ported.
decisions.evidence: build-34: 0 compiler errors, 0 new warnings, objects 7,371 -> 7,372; nm vmlinux shows mtk_smi_clk_enable/mtk_smi_clk_disable/mtk_smi_dev_get/mtk_smi_conf_set/smi_bus_prepare_enable/smi_bus_disable_unprepare/smi_get_dev_num as T with 7 __ksymtab_* entries; strings on the object list mediatek,smi_common / mediatek,smi_larb / mediatek,smi_sub_common / mediatek,smi-id / clock-names; hwenable bind audit: mediatek,smi_common nodes=1 and mediatek,smi_larb nodes=5 both class ENABLED with driver=drivers/memory/mtk-smi-mt6768.c, CONFIG_MTK_SMI_MT6768=y; clkaudit --require-fresh totals unchanged at {refs:234, registered:234, unresolved_provider:0}, CLK_MM row 37/37 and SCP_SYS row 23/23, so every clock cell the six SMI nodes reference is already registered by patch 0074's clk-mt6768.c/clk-mt6768-pg.c; sha256 of mt6768.dtb identical to build-33 (34a7e6b536a3a34e...), i.e. the DT was not modified
decisions.status: done this round (substrate only; M4U is the next increment)

decisions.decision: Give the ported SMI API its own header include/soc/mediatek/smi-mt6768.h instead of extending <soc/mediatek/smi.h> as the BSP does.
decisions.why: The first build failed with 6 errors: this tree also builds mainline's drivers/memory/mtk-smi.c (CONFIG_MTK_SMI=y since an earlier round), which defines its own static mtk_smi_clk_enable()/mtk_smi_clk_disable() for its struct mtk_smi, so a shared header produced 'static declaration of mtk_smi_clk_enable follows non-static declaration' plus four incompatible-pointer-type errors. The BSP avoids this only because it puts its mainline-shaped SMI code (those statics included) inside #if !IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_MTK_SMI_EXT) - in the BSP one of the two drivers is never compiled. A 5.15 tree has both as separate files, so the names must not share a header; splitting keeps mainline's driver intact for SoCs whose DT matches it.
decisions.evidence: build-34 log after the split: 0 errors; nm vmlinux shows both 't mtk_smi_clk_enable' (mainline's static, in drivers/memory/mtk-smi.c) and 'T mtk_smi_clk_enable' (this driver) side by side; include/soc/mediatek/smi.h left byte-identical to build-33 (44 lines, git checkout -- was used to undo the first attempt)

decisions.decision: Do not port the BSP's smi_register() (smi_drv.c:1330-1393), its BWC table/debugfs/misc-device surface, or the register_pg_callback() MTCMOS re-enable hook; record them as deferred work with their consequences. The mtk_smi_conf_set() BWC register writes are left in but inert.
decisions.why: smi_register() cannot run against this DT as written: it does of_parse_phandle(smi_dev[SMI_LARB_NUM]->dev->of_node, "mmsys_config", 0) and returns -ENOMEM when that phandle property is absent, and this board's smi_common@14002000 node does not carry it (adding it would be the speculative DT surgery the rules forbid). Its remaining work is bandwidth control (BWC tables, sysfs, mmdvfs/PMQOS, mmprofile, sspm), none of which affects whether M4U/display clients can bind. The consequence is stated rather than stubbed: larb clocks come up when a client calls smi_bus_prepare_enable() instead of being pre-enabled at init, no larb is left enabled by the driver itself, and an SMI clock lost across a subsystem power cycle is not restored by this file because the after_on/before_off pg hook is absent.
decisions.evidence: vendor smi_drv.c:1354-1360 (the mmsys_config phandle lookup and its -ENOMEM), packaged DT dump lines 3445-3475 (smi_common@14002000: compatible/reg/mediatek,smi-id only, no mmsys_config property); mtk_smi_conf_set() loops over nr_conf_pairs/nr_scen_pairs, both 0 since smi_conf_get() was not ported, so the function writes nothing instead of writing a partial set
decisions.status: deferred on purpose, tracked in KNOWN-ISSUES.md

decisions.decision: Fix bin/hwenable.py to index DTB compatibles per NUL-separated string rather than per property blob, and re-derive the bind audit.
decisions.why: This board's DTB stores multi-entry compatibles as one blob ('mediatek,smi_larb0\0mediatek,smi_larb', 'mediatek,scpsys\0syscon'), which dtc prints with \0 inside a single quoted string. of_match_node() tests every NUL-terminated entry, so a driver binding on the second entry looked driverless to the audit - which is exactly how the five new SMI larb nodes would have been reported no-driver while the driver really matches them. The audit is the acceptance test for 'every ported binding matches a node that exists in the packaged DTB', so it had to be corrected rather than worked around.
decisions.evidence: before (hw.json): 413 nodes with compatible / 339 distinct / 22 bound / 16 enabled / 4 enableable / 317 driverless, and no row for 'mediatek,smi_larb' at all; after (rows re-run): 450 / 349 / 33 bound / 24 enabled / 5 enableable / 316 driverless, 'mediatek,smi_larb' nodes=5 class ENABLED, +42 rows from split entries; mediatek,m4u nodes=1 class NO_DRIVER (the M4U port is what removes that one)
decisions.status: tool fixed, report/hardware-enablement.rows.md + .json regenerated from build-34
